description:
## Goal

Give generated callable identities exact source ownership across live function replacement, without using display labels or interner order as semantic authority.

## Reproducer and evidence

Discovered during fz-tfn.18's real same-body contribution test. In one Compiler2, submit same_body_contributions.fz containing:

fn main() do
  dbg(:retained)
  f = fn x -> x + 1 end
  dbg(f)
  1
end

Request and interpret main/0; then replace the same named source with the same body except final result 2 and interpret the retained root again.

The second request panics: "distinct callable identities require distinct stable labels". Backtrace from focused run 26192: Types::name_callable (types/mod.rs around2105) <- World::define_generated_function (world.rs around3070) <- Lowerer::lower_lambda (around2572), during source reconciliation before new root packaging.

At predecessor 2f91336cd the same name_callable, define_generated_function and lower_lambda authority exists. The .18 diff changes world.rs only to pass Types into macro runtime argument encoding; it does not change generated-function registration or the Types label invariant. An executable baseline reproduction on that predecessor has not yet been run; preserve this distinction from source-level attribution.

World::define_generated_function uses reference_generated(owner, owner_module, surface.span, arity), then registers a stable callable label. Replacing source can mint a distinct generated identity with a label already owned by a retained older identity. Do not resolve this by raw-ID tie-breaking, display-string identity, deleting the uniqueness assertion without replacing its invariant, or relabeling old interned types.

## Strategy and TDD

1. Reproduce the two-request failure independently of root contribution packaging, and pin predecessor behavior with the smallest source/lowering test.
2. Trace generated identity, source/span ownership, stable label registration and retained older closures/types. Decide from semantics which facts identify the same denotation and which distinguish genuinely changed lambdas.
3. Repair the owning data model. Preserve old closures/snapshots while giving live replacements coherent identities. Remove any duplicate naming/identity mechanism made obsolete.
4. Test unchanged inline lambda plus an unrelated enclosing arithmetic edit; genuinely changed lambda body; insertion/reordering of sibling lambdas; named-function-reference control; retained old callable behavior; same-version deterministic artifacts and diagnostics.
5. Verify interp/native/AOT behavior and exact invalidation/reuse. Update type/source/callable docs from final code; full applicable gates, cold ticket-scoped review, one commit/close.

## Ordering

Tail issue discovered during .18, not permission to weaken that ticket. .18 proves same-body equal atom/wrapper retention using a named function reference with a stable existing callable identity, plus direct production reconciliation tests. The inline-lambda failure happens in source lowering before packaging; it is not repaired as an incidental .18 change. If independent evidence establishes that .18's required packaging cutover depends on this repair, update dependencies and resolve it first. Epic final cleanup remains blocked on this issue.
title: Preserve coherent generated callable identity across live source replacement
